Definition: from a derivative of the same as G4435; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively):--fight.
BiblicalUsage: Pykteo means to box, to fight with the fists as at the games. It appears once, and Paul uses it of himself: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly, so fight I, not as one that beateth the air.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul's boxing is the picture of a disciplined life: he does not swing at the air, he aims every blow, because he is fighting for a crown.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
